subject: Maths
title: Adding and subtracting surds
subtitle: Surds · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can add and subtract surds by collecting like surd terms.

key_vocab.definition: A surd is an irrational root such as √2 or √5. We can only add or subtract surds that have the same number under the root sign (like terms).

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can add and subtract surds by collecting like surd terms.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: surd -- A surd is an irrational root such as √2 or √5. We can only add or subtract surds that have the same number under the root sign (like terms).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Only like surds (same radicand) can be added or subtracted. Simplify surds first to reveal like terms.
a√n + b√n = (a + b)√n
Collect like surd terms

Key examples:
  ✓ 3√5 + 2√5 = 5√5  (like surds, add coefficients)
  ✓ √12 + √3 = 2√3 + √3 = 3√3  (simplify first)
  ✓ 7√2 - 4√2 = 3√2  (subtract coefficients)
  ✗ √3 + √5 = √8  (cannot add unlike surds under one root)
  ✗ 2√3 + 3√2 = 5√5  (different surds cannot be combined)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – like surds
  Simplify 4√3 + 7√3.
  Both terms have √3
  Add coefficients: 4 + 7 = 11
  = 11√3
  11√3
  (Treat surds like algebra: add the coefficients of like terms.)

Example 2 – subtraction
  Simplify 9√2 - 5√2.
  Both terms have √2
  Subtract coefficients: 9 - 5 = 4
  = 4√2
  4√2
  (Same process for subtraction.)

sections.title: Simplify first, then combine
sections.content:
Simplify each surd, then add or subtract.

(a) √12 + √3
(b) √20 + √5
(c) √27 - √3
(d) √45 + √20
